name: v9.1.0
body:
rqbit 9.1.0 is mostly a stability and correctness release, with a few small features. Several fixes stop a remote peer from crashing rqbit: deeply nested bencode, an out-of-range ut_metadata request, and a panic in the incoming-connection listener. It also adds `socks5h://` proxies, fixes BEP 52 hybrid torrents that couldn't be added, and fixes a web UI bug that cut output folder names at `#`.

**Library users:** `PeerConnectionOptions` has a new `max_request_window` field. If you build that struct with every field listed instead of using `..Default::default()`, add the new field.

## Features
* Support `socks5h://` proxy URLs by @jpds in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/683
* Make the per-peer request window configurable by @melkir in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/687
* Stats: count connected peers that have the full torrent by @zond in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/649

## Crash and security fixes
* bencode: limit deserializer recursion depth (remote stack-overflow abort) by @tweedge in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/660
* Fix off-by-one in ut_metadata bounds check (remote panic) by @MarcelCoding in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/704
* Don't panic in listener accept by @ikatson in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/674

## Fixes
* Torrents: don't reject duplicate `.pad/<length>` filenames, so BEP 52 hybrid torrents can be added, by @tweedge in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/701
* Web UI: output folder no longer truncated at `#` when adding torrents, by @qnfm in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/710
* Docker: make the CA cert bundle world-readable, so the image runs as a non-root user, by @Allypost in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/712
* Route blocklist/allowlist downloads through the proxied client by @jpds in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/669
* Peers: detect capabilities from the handshake on incoming connections by @zond in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/651
* Peers: accept an extended handshake missing the `m` dictionary by @jpds in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/684
* Peers: read the handshake until it is complete by @ArshPunisher in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/699
* DHT: fix duplicate `request_one` call by @moshen in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/646
* DHT: keep the worker alive after a per-datagram recv error on Windows by @nickEatsBread in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/690
* LSD: cancel the announce task once the torrent is removed by @lvella in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/700
* Storage: write past 2 GiB where pwritev takes a 32-bit `off_t` by @zond in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/661
* Windows: mark files sparse regardless of the log level by @tvollstaedt in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/681
* Release the state lock before `update_only_files` touches the peer table by @zond in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/659
* Take a piece out of the download queue once we have it by @zond in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/655
* Only treat 40-character hex strings as info hashes by @melkir in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/688
* Streaming: wait for the initial check in `ManagedTorrent::stream` by @melkir in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/689
* Storage API: don't lose `is_type_id` through boxing and wrapping (#652), forward `pwrite_all_vectored` through `Box` (#654), and forward `on_piece_completed` through the storage middlewares (#653), all by @zond
* Core: `CurrentPiece::piece_offset` is now the offset within the piece by @MemoDo-En in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/695
* Build: use `.PHONY` instead of `@PHONY` in Makefiles by @TUKAIL in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/676
* Dependencies updated (#716)

## New Contributors
@moshen, @zond, @tweedge, @jpds, @TUKAIL, @tvollstaedt, @melkir, @nickEatsBread, @ArshPunisher, @MarcelCoding, @Allypost, @qnfm, @lvella and @MemoDo-En made their first contributions. Thank you!

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/compare/v9.0.1...v9.1.0

### Major changes since [v9.0.0-beta.0](https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/releases/tag/v9.0.0-beta.0) (where uTP support is the main change)
- Full IPv6 support. Rqbit now runs everything in dualstack IPv6 + IPv4 mode by default. It can also work in pure-IPv6 mode just fine. This could discover and connect to more peers.
- ```rqbit download``` is now completely stateless and doesn't use the same ports as ```rqbit server``` does. This makes it very easy to run multiple concurrent instances.

name: v9.0.0-beta.0
body:
# Major new rqbit release 9.0.0-beta.0

The are some major new features and some breaking changes in the API / CLI.

## TLDR
- rqbit now supports uTP protocol, which will help discovering more peers. Enable via ```--experimental-enable-utp-listen```. I'll probably enable it by default once 9.0.0 full is released.
- breaking CLI change: you need to replace ```--tcp-min(max)-port``` with ```--listen-port``` if you used those.
- breaking librqbit changes: some SessionOptions are moved around

## uTP support
After a long wait, we finally have support for [uTP (uTorrent transport protocol)](https://www.bittorrent.org/beps/bep_0029.html) done through specially created [librqbit-utp](https://github.com/ikatson/librqbit-utp/) library.

What does that mean for end users? Mostly, that you'll get more peer connections, especially on torrents with low seed count. It turns out that in the wild there's lots of peers that only have uTP enabled, but they don't listen on TCP. For those torrents previously rqbit couldn't connect to those peers at all.

This turned out to be one of the hardest pieces of code I've ever written, it's pretty much as complex as creating a TCP stack from scratch.

There are some caveats though, which is why uTP is disabled by default and you need to enable it explicitly via ```--experimental-enable-utp-listen```.

## uTP caveats
**First**, the original reason for uTP creation was LEDBAT congestion control algorithm, which is notably missing from the current implementation, and we use CUBIC (the modern TCP congestion control algorithm) instead. I'll probably add LEDBAT someday, it shouldn't be hard. The reasoning behind LEDBAT is to move torrent traffic to background so that it doesn't interfere with normal network operation on the machine. In practice, in my network conditions this is never an issue: I never notice rqbit slowing down my internet to make it noticeable.

**Second**, the librqbit-utp code is complex and there might be bugs. It seems stable for me, hence I'm making this release: I was running my rqbit for a while in uTP-only mode. But **I'm asking all users to please try it out and report issues**.

**Third**, although I tried hard optimizing it, it can't beat kernel's TCP stacks that were being optimized for tens of years by very talented engineers. TCP runs in the kernel, while uTP in tokio userspace. For this reason, rqbit first tries connecting over TCP, and only if it doesn't work after 1 second, a uTP connection attempt is made.

uTP can saturate my gigabit connection however on Apple devices, so it's not slow, just slower than TCP at the limits, and also noticeable on slower devices. E.g. my OpenWrt router can squeeze ~50 megabytes/s with TCP, but only about 20-25 over uTP. Of course it can be optimized further and it's just the beginning.

**One more caveat** is UDP socket read buffer is shared among all connections, unlike TCP (which is per connection). librqbit-utp tries to increase SO_RCVBUF, but it's likely to fail increasing it enough at least on Linux. This can result in lost incoming packets which will make uTP work considerably worse with fast download speeds, so to prevent this you might need to increase ```/proc/sys/net/rmem_max``` on Linux.

## Prometheus metrics exporter
While creating librqbit-utp it proved extremely handy to monitor it using metrics, as logs would be too verbose and have too much overhead.

So I added prometheus metrics available under ```/metrics``` HTTP endpoint. For now there's only uTP metrics, but we can add more to rqbit itself.

## Other changes including breaking
- added ```--listen-port```, ```--listen-ip```, ```--enable-prometheus-exporter``` options
- breaking: env / CLI: ```RQBIT_TCP_LISTEN_MIN_PORT (--tcp-min-port)``` and ```RQBIT_TCP_LISTEN_MAX_PORT (--tcp-max-port)``` moved to ```RQBIT_LISTEN_PORT```
- breaking: librqbit SessionOptions: ```peer_opts``` and ```socks_proxy_url``` moved to ```opts: Option<ConnectionOptions>```
- breaking: librqbit SessionOptions: ```enable_upnp_port_forwarding``` moved to ```listen: Option<ListenerOptions>```

## What's Changed
* Use Rust edition 2024 by @ikatson in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/377
* librqbit: backoff crate (unmaintained) -> backon by @ikatson in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/378
* uTP support (disabled by default) by @ikatson in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/322
* Preparing 9.0.0-beta.0 release by @ikatson in https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/pull/379

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit/compare/v8.1.0...v9.0.0-beta.0
